_note: The airport walk (components/fly/AirportWalk): you walk the departures terminal yourself, the way you would for real: find your flight on the departures board, drop your bag at your airline's check-in row, passport control's e-gates, security (what goes in the tray, your bag on the X-ray belt, through the arch), then find your gate from your boarding pass and board. Each airport has its own look, gate letter, landmark and real-life tips (general advice: always check your own airline and airport). parSeconds: the time for three stars. Scores are kept on the device only; nothing here pays money. style: the airport's architecture (components/fly/AirportStyle). country: the country it's in (countries: its rules, shown when you arrive from another country). You live in the UAE, so at UAE airports the e-gates read your Emirates ID; in Qatar you're a visitor and an officer checks you at the desk (desk: what they ask). A flight inside one country (Dubai to Abu Dhabi) is domestic: no passport control or customs.

dubai.intro: Dubai International is one of the world's busiest airports for international passengers. Terminal 3 has a giant duty-free hall under its arched roof.

tips.board: Arrive about 3 hours before an international flight. The departures screens show your flight's check-in row and, later, your gate.
tips.checkin: Check-in usually closes 60 minutes before departure. Many airlines let you check in online and just drop your bag at the counter.
tips.passport: You live in the UAE, so the Smart Gates are for you: scan your Emirates ID or passport and look at the camera. No officer needed. (Visitors may be sent to a desk.)
tips.security: Laptops, liquids and anything metal go in the tray. Liquids must be in containers of 100 ml or less, all in one clear bag.
tips.gate: Some Terminal 3 gates (the A gates) are reached by a short automated train. Boarding usually starts 45 to 60 minutes before departure, and gates close about 20 minutes before.

tips.immigration: UAE residents and many visitors use the Smart Gates. First-time visitors may be sent to a desk, where an officer checks their visa and passport.
tips.baggage: The screens in the reclaim hall show which belt has your flight's bags. Many suitcases look alike: check the tag before you take one.
tips.customs: Nothing to declare? Take the green channel. Cash and valuables over AED 60,000 must be declared, and bags can still be X-rayed on the way out.
tips.exit: Outside arrivals: the taxi rank, ride apps and, at Terminals 1 and 3, the Dubai Metro Red Line into the city.

customsQuiz.q: Which of these must you declare at Dubai customs?
customsQuiz.why: Cash and valuables over AED 60,000 (or the same in other currencies) must be declared. Your own laptop, phone and a duty-free gift are fine.

desk.say: The officer scans your Emirates ID: “Welcome home.”
The officer scans your Emirates ID: “Welcome, have a good trip.”

abu-dhabi.intro: Abu Dhabi's Terminal A opened in 2023: one huge, bright hall under a curved roof, with the piers fanning out from the middle.

tips.board: Find your flight on the departures screens first: they show the check-in row for your flight and when check-in closes.
tips.checkin: Have your passport ready. Power banks and spare batteries must go in your cabin bag, never in the bag you check in.
tips.passport: UAE residents use the biometric e-gates: your face is matched to your Emirates ID or passport. Keep looking at the camera until the gate opens.
tips.security: Take your laptop and tablet out of your bag, and put your phone, keys, belt and coins in the tray. Big water bottles have to be emptied or thrown away.
tips.gate: Read your gate on your boarding pass, then follow the overhead signs. Gate numbers can change, so check the screens again on the way.

tips.immigration: Abu Dhabi's biometric gates match your face to your passport: look at the camera until the gate opens.
tips.baggage: Find your flight number on the belt screens. If your bag doesn't come, report it at the baggage desk before you leave the hall.
tips.customs: The green channel is for nothing to declare, the red one for goods or cash over AED 60,000. Prescription medicines should come with the prescription.
tips.exit: Taxis wait outside arrivals; the city centre is about 30 minutes away.

customsQuiz.q: You're bringing your own prescription medicine. What should you carry with it?
customsQuiz.why: Some medicines are controlled in the UAE. Carry the prescription (and keep them in their boxes) so customs can see they're yours.

desk.say: The officer scans your Emirates ID: “Welcome back to the UAE.”
The officer scans your Emirates ID: “Welcome, have a good trip.”

doha.intro: Hamad International is Qatar's hub. Its duty-free hall is famous for a giant yellow teddy bear sculpture, and it has an indoor tropical garden called the Orchard.

tips.board: Qatar is a different country from the UAE: you need the right visa or entry permit before you fly. The screens show your check-in row.
tips.checkin: Weigh your bag before you leave home: going over your allowance costs extra at the counter.
tips.passport: Hamad's e-gates are for Qatar residents (and some eligible passports). As a visitor from the UAE, go to an officer's desk: have your passport and visa ready.
tips.security: Anything metal sets off the arch: take off your belt and watch, and put your phone and keys in the tray.
tips.gate: Hamad's gates are spread over concourses A to E, with a train between some of them. Leave time to walk: some gates are a long way from the duty-free hall.

tips.immigration: You're a visitor in Qatar, so queue for an officer's desk (the e-gates are for Qatar residents). Have your passport, visa and hotel booking ready.
tips.baggage: Check the screens for your flight's belt. Trolleys are free at Hamad: grab one for big bags.
tips.customs: Cash over QAR 50,000 must be declared. Alcohol and pork products can't be brought into Qatar.
tips.exit: The Doha Metro Red Line runs from the airport into the city, and taxis and ride apps wait outside.

customsQuiz.q: Which of these can't you bring into Qatar?
customsQuiz.why: Alcohol can't be brought into Qatar (and neither can pork products). Cash over QAR 50,000 must be declared.

desk.say: “Welcome to Qatar. Purpose of your visit?” The officer checks your passport and visa, takes your photo and stamps you in.

quiz.q: “Where are you staying?” What should you have ready?

options.text: My hotel booking (or my host's address) and return ticket
A photo of the Doha skyline

quiz.why: Visitors to Qatar need their accommodation details (a hotel booking or a host's address) for their visa or entry, and should have their return or onward ticket ready.

desk.say: The officer checks your passport, your visa and the date you came in, then stamps you out.

quiz.q: “Your visa ends tomorrow,” says the officer. What happens if a visitor stays past it?

options.text: A fine for every extra day, and you can't leave until it's paid
Nothing: visit visas don't run out
Just a warning the first time

quiz.why: Overstaying a visa (in Qatar and in the UAE) means a fine for each extra day, and you can be stopped at the airport until it's paid. Leave, or extend it, before it runs out.

checkinQuiz.q: Your power bank: where does it go?

options.text: In my cabin bag, with me
In the suitcase I check in

checkinQuiz.why: Lithium batteries can overheat. In the cabin the crew can deal with it, so power banks and spare batteries always fly with you, never in the hold.

securityItems.label: Laptop
securityItems.why: Laptops and tablets come out of the bag and go in a tray on their own.

securityItems.label: Liquids bag (all under 100 ml)
securityItems.why: Your clear bag of small liquids goes in the tray so the officer can see it.

securityItems.label: Phone, keys & coins
securityItems.why: Metal sets off the arch, so pockets go in the tray.

securityItems.label: Full 500 ml water bottle
securityItems.why: Over 100 ml isn't allowed through security: empty it or bin it, and fill up after.

securityItems.label: A book
securityItems.why: Books can stay in your bag.

baggage._note: Check-in's scale: your suitcase's weight against your cabin's allowance (kg). Over it: pay excessPerKg (AED) for each kg over, or repack into your cabin bag (it starts at cabinStart kg and may not go over cabinLimit).
baggage.tip: Weigh your suitcase at home. Excess baggage is usually much cheaper if you add it online before you fly than at the counter.

UAE.name: the UAE
UAE.domestic: Dubai to Abu Dhabi is a domestic flight, inside the UAE: no passport control and no customs. Just show your Emirates ID or passport at the gate.

rules.text: Declare cash or valuables worth over AED 60,000 at customs.
Some medicines are controlled: bring the prescription, in the original box.
Don't photograph or film people without their permission: it's against the law.
Alcohol only in licensed places, never in public, and zero tolerance for drink-driving.
Dress modestly in malls, government buildings and mosques: shoulders and knees covered.
You can't bring alcohol or pork products into Qatar.
E-cigarettes and vapes are banned in Qatar: leave them at home.
Declare cash or valuables worth over QAR 50,000.
Some medicines are controlled: carry the prescription with them.
Dress modestly in public places: shoulders and knees covered.
Keep your passport, visa and hotel booking with you, and leave before your visa runs out.
